_meta.purpose: Vendored subset of public APK protection detection signatures (DEX, native, manifest). Used by the re-apktool classify_apk_protection tool. Vendor-neutral: only category labels, no product / publisher / app names.

category_legend.apk_packager: The APK was assembled by a 3rd-party packager that obscures the original package layout.
category_legend.dex_obfuscator: The DEX classes were processed by a Java/Kotlin obfuscator (name-rename + control-flow flatten + string-encrypt).
category_legend.native_vm_bytecode_interpreter: A native .so was wrapped by an encrypted-VM bytecode interpreter; classes.dex is a thin shim.
category_legend.anti_tamper_runtime: A native .so contains a runtime integrity / debugger / emulator detection surface.
category_legend.string_encryption: The DEX string pool was processed by a string-encryptor that the consumer must decrypt before reading.
category_legend.resource_encryption: The APK resources were processed by a resource-encryptor; resources.arsc is opaque without the matching decryptor.
category_legend.anti_debug_native: A native .so contains anti-debug primitives (ptrace self-attach, /proc/status walk, signal-mask probe).
category_legend.anti_frida_native: A native .so contains Frida-gadget detection (port scan, library walk, dlsym lookup).
category_legend.root_detection: The APK or its native libs probe for Magisk / SuperSU / su binary.
category_legend.ssl_pinning: The network code uses OkHttp / TrustManager / NetworkSecurityConfig to pin certificates.

evidence_legend.class_name: DEX class with a non-obfuscated name (the obfuscator's seed names tend to be a single letter or symbol).
evidence_legend.method_signature: DEX method signature with a known-encrypted prefix.
evidence_legend.string_literal: DEX or native lib contains a string literal that is the canonical signal.
evidence_legend.native_section: A .so has a section name (or absence of expected section) that signals the protection class.
evidence_legend.manifest_meta: The AndroidManifest.xml has a meta-data tag that the packager / obfuscator adds.
evidence_legend.file_path: An APK file is at a path that signals the protection class (e.g. /lib/.../lib<packager-name>.so).

source_credits: https://github.com/rednaga/APKiD (APKiD open signatures for DEX/native/manifest protection detection)

entries.note: Meta-data tag in AndroidManifest.xml that a known APK packager adds. Multiple packager tags on one APK = the APK was re-packed.

entries.match_pattern: single-letter class names (a, b, c, aa, ab, ...)
entries.note: Class names in classes.dex that are 1-2 letters are a strong obfuscator signal. Counter-example: some legitimate frameworks also use 1-2 letter names (kotlin.coroutines.intrinsics); review the package prefix.

entries.match_pattern: method bodies with only 1-3 instructions + a single call to a static decrypt stub
entries.note: Method bodies that are just 'invoke-static decrypt-stub' are a control-flow-flattened string-decrypt pattern.

entries.match_pattern: presence of a 'Decrypt' or 'd' class with a single static 'd(String)' method
entries.note: The canonical string-decrypt stub. The obfuscator rewrites every string-literal load as a call to this method.

entries.match_pattern: lib<obfuscated>.so with a non-standard .text section (small, low entropy) and a large .data or .bss (high entropy)
entries.note: Native encrypted-VM bytecode interpreter shape: the interpreter + dispatcher are in .text (small, normal entropy); the encrypted handlers are in .data / .bss (large, high entropy). The .init_array entry point is the lazy-decrypt stub.

Strings that indicate the native lib is searching for Frida gadget or frida-server. Note: these strings are not in the catalog (they are matched at runtime); the catalog only describes the *category*.
The canonical Linux anti-debug primitive: read /proc/self/status, look for 'TracerPid: 0'. Used by native-side anti-debug in modern Android apps.
Native-side Frida detection: scan /proc/self/maps for the frida-agent library, scan TCP for the default 27042 port.
Strings that indicate the app probes for root: check for the su binary, the Magisk mount, the Superuser.apk package. High FP in apps that legitimately interact with root (e.g. system tools).
OkHttp CertificatePinner is the canonical SSL-pinning pattern. The bypass is to override the pin check in OkHttp's CertificatePinner class.
The AndroidManifest declares a networkSecurityConfig XML that pins certs. The bypass is to repackage the APK with an empty networkSecurityConfig.

entries.match_pattern: resources.arsc is opaque, .arsc decryption stub in DEX
entries.note: The .arsc is encrypted; the obfuscator's decrypt stub must be called before the resources can be read. Pair with apk-004 (string-encryption stub).
